identity.description: L1-penalized least squares: the soft-thresholding geometry of the L1 ball zeroes coefficients exactly, so the fitted model IS a feature selection — the surviving support is the effect story. Fit by cyclic coordinate descent.

axes.note: cyclic coordinate descent is deterministic; selection='random' is the only stochastic mode

emits.note: POINT ESTIMATES ONLY (no SEs; post-selection inference is a research topic, not a library call). The zero pattern doubles as a feature-selection mask — no dedicated port type exists; portTypeProposal: 'feature-mask' if selection composition becomes a template

alpha.note: controls the sparsity level directly; above a data-dependent alpha_max ALL coefficients are zero

max_iter.note: raise on ConvergenceWarning — common near tiny alpha or with unscaled inputs

selection.note: 'random' can converge faster at high tol but makes the fit stochastic

invariances.why: the L1 threshold is applied in raw coefficient units — WHICH features survive selection depends on their units, so unscaled input makes the selection itself arbitrary, not just the magnitudes
linear in the inputs; monotone transforms change both the fit and the selected support
coordinate descent has no missing-value path; NaN raises
requires a pre-encoded numeric design matrix
squared-error loss presumes a linear mean (Gaussian MLE view); additionally the sparsity 'bet' — that the true signal concentrates in few features — is itself an assumption
designed for wide data: defined at p >> n, though it can then select at most n features by the KKT conditions
the (sparse) linear predictor extends unboundedly beyond the training range

featureStats.why: within a correlated group the L1 geometry picks ONE member near-arbitrarily and zeroes the rest — high correlation means the selected support is unstable (the elastic-net handoff signal)
the sparsity prior earns its keep at large p; mechanically, with p > n at most n features can be selected
the L1 bet pays only if the true signal is concentrated in few features — a dense-signal problem is better served by ridge's shrink-everything geometry

modelMetrics.why: Jaccard overlap of the selected support across CV folds — low overlap means the 'selected features' narrative is noise, even if CV error looks fine
the realized sparsity at the tuned alpha; zero survivors means alpha overshot into the intercept-only model and the fit is vacuous

edgeCases.behavior: selects one member near-arbitrarily, zeroes the rest; support flips between refits
edgeCases.note: elastic_net is the designed fix (grouping effect)

edgeCases.behavior: all coefficients zero — intercept-only model returned silently
at most n features can enter the support (KKT), regardless of how many are truly relevant

edgeCases.condition: ConvergenceWarning at max_iter (tiny alpha or unscaled X)
edgeCases.behavior: coefficients from an unconverged coordinate-descent pass

driver.threadSafety: single-threaded coordinate descent; predict is thread-safe

canBeSeeds.note: bagged lasso (~stability selection) directly attacks the support-instability weakness

placementClaims.why: no native NaN path — coordinate descent raises on missing values
linearizing skewed covariates improves the linear-mean fit and keeps leverage points from steering the selection
the L1 threshold is unit-dependent — without standardization the SELECTION (not just the magnitudes) is an artifact of units
categoricals must be design-encoded; note one-hot groups are then selected member-wise, not as a group
